Revenue / Subscription expansion

Expansion MRR from existing accounts

The total positive monthly recurring-revenue increments from accounts paying at the start of the measurement period. Each eligible recurring-value change is counted once in the movement ledger.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The total positive monthly recurring-revenue increments from accounts paying at the start of the measurement period. Each eligible recurring-value change is counted once in the movement ledger.

currency/month

How we use it

We connect customer adoption, seat growth, upgrades, and recurring add-ons to existing-account growth.

Transparent calculationSum of positive monthly normalized recurring-revenue increments for eligible existing paying accounts
eligible positive mrr increments1,500; 2,500; 1,000

1,500 + 2,500 + 1,000 = 5,000 currency units/month of expansion MRR.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Account and starting cohort
  • Upgrade, seat, or add-on movement
  • Plan and customer segment

Questions we investigate

  • Which expansion motions create recurring value?
  • Are movements duplicated or offset later?
  • Does growth come from established accounts?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Reconcile upgrades to the recurring ledger.
  • Compare expansion with contraction and churn.
  • Support adoption before proposing relevant upgrades.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Revenue operations and finance leads
Monthly after billing normalization and reconciliation.

Required data

  • Deduplicated positive MRR movement IDs
  • Starting-period paying account membership
  • Monthly normalization and currency rules

Read the measure with context

An empty eligible set totals zero. Exclude new-logo MRR and one-off charges; document reactivation treatment. Contraction is tracked separately. Billing frequency, discounts, refunds, and duplicate movements can distort the total without normalization.
